items.text: Foreign ministers of several Arab and Islamic countries condemned Israel's opposition to Donald Trump's comprehensive plan to end the Gaza war. The plan was approved in UN Security Council resolution 2803. They stated that Israel's opposition is the main obstacle to peace efforts in Gaza and Palestine.

The commander of the US Central Command announced that the Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier group is returning home after more than 260 days of mission in the Arabian Sea. The group shot down over 200 IRGC drones during operations against the Islamic Republic. The CENTCOM commander also mentioned the pressures of the long mission on the crew and their families.

The Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar emphasized the need for adherence to negotiation and diplomacy in a phone call with the Syrian Foreign Minister. They stressed ensuring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and maintaining regional security. Qatar expressed full support for efforts to reduce tensions and achieve lasting peace.

Hamas called on mediator countries to compel Israel to implement the first phase of the Gaza ceasefire commitments after meeting with Jared Kushner. This request was made following talks in Cairo. Kushner is scheduled to meet Netanyahu to discuss stopping attacks and implementing the second phase of the agreement.

Anti-war protesters in South Korea gathered in front of the US embassy demanding the halt of the annual joint military exercise. The protest followed Trump's order to significantly reduce the scale of the exercises. The "Freedom Shield Ulchi" exercise with about 18,000 South Korean troops has started.

The Hengaw human rights organization reported that 16 people arrested in autumn 2024 were sentenced to a total of 77 years and 9 months in prison. They were accused of charges such as gathering and collusion, membership in PJAK, and propaganda against the regime. These individuals were denied access to lawyers and family visits during detention.

The share of US oil in South Korea's crude oil imports exceeded 20 percent in the first half of the year for the first time. The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and disruption in Middle East oil supply has pushed South Korean refineries toward alternative sources.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Iranian leaders are preparing the Revolutionary Guard and proxy groups to increase pressure on Washington and its allies during negotiations with the US. Iran has increased the Guard's control over the army and expanded missile and drone production. The Guard is also considering plans to escalate regional attacks and believes the main war has not yet begun.

Mohammad Jafar Ghaempanah explained that under sanctions, oil must be sold illegally and payment may be delayed or never returned. He mentioned issues such as timing of sales, payment return, and cargo safety. The government is working to lift sanctions to end these problems and profiteering.

Reza Akrami stated that some war damages to the country are temporary while others affect infrastructure and take time to repair. He emphasized the need to support the government to resolve issues faster. He also said that Iran's current priority is defending the country and confronting enemies.

The Iranian Women's Premier Football League is set to start in three weeks. Various controversies have arisen before the league begins. Raha Pourbakhsh discussed these issues on the Hat-trick program.

The Wall Street Journal, citing Iranian and Arab officials, reported that the leaders of the Islamic Republic have prepared to expand the war over the past two months. Actions include increasing the influence of the Revolutionary Guards, changing commanders, increasing missile and drone production, and coordinating with proxy forces. This report was published by Amir Giti from Iran International.

Iranians living in Calgary held their 32nd week of protests outside the city hall in support of prisoners facing execution in Iran. The protesters called for greater attention from the international community and Canadian media to the executions and the situation of political prisoners. They pointed to the ongoing repression following the December protests.

Hossein Ghazian stated that the gap between society and rulers has deepened over the past two decades. He said the government uses tools such as street repression, executions, and restricting education to control society. This indicates an increasing distance between the new generations and the government.

The representative of Tafresh in the parliament stated that the White House officials should consider the consequences of turning conflicts into a regional war. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic will not surrender to threats and will respond decisively. He also noted that the military power of the US alone cannot achieve its political goals.

Mohammad Qaedi stated that despite a reduction in some provocative actions, about 28,500 American troops remain in South Korea. Washington has also maintained its nuclear commitment to South Korea and Japan. This indicates that the US does not intend to significantly reduce its deterrence level in the region.

Amir Hamidi stated that the aggressive rhetoric of the Islamic Republic officials does not reflect the real balance of power and aims to strengthen deterrence and Tehran's bargaining position. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic can impose costs and regional crises but does not have strategic superiority over the US. The current situation is a fragile balance between deterrence, pressure, and indirect diplomacy, with a serious risk of conflict resumption.

Gholamreza Nouri Ghezeljeh, Minister of Agriculture, stated that the government has faced continuous crises over the past two years. Despite the naval blockade and ongoing war, food security and commodity stocks remain stable. He also emphasized that the war has increased costs and the final prices of goods.

Hossein Samsami, a member of the Parliament's Economic Commission, called the increase of gasoline prices to 87,000 tomans a sign of mismanagement and said these plans cause public unrest. He warned that this price hike could lead to the closure of businesses like Snapp and taxis. He also emphasized that these plans have severe social impacts and lead to social unrest.

Morteza Kazemian from Iran International stated that the Islamic Republic has no motivation to end tensions with the US and emphasizes its military approach in the Strait of Hormuz. He warned that this approach is based on the assumption of suppressing protests and controlling civil society.

The family and relatives of Saeed Tarvand gathered by his grave on his birthday anniversary. Saeed Tarvand, a 33-year-old oil company contractor, was killed during the December 18 protests in Abadan. He was buried in Mehran County, Ilam Province.

A group of Iranians living in Austin, Texas held a rally on Sunday, August 16. They demanded the Trump administration stop negotiations with the Islamic Republic. They also condemned the execution of protesters in Iran.

Donald Trump considered the signing of a joint defense pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan as a sign of unity in the Middle East. He welcomed the pact. More details were reported by Javad Hamdani.

Rodri, the captain of the Spanish national team, has joined Barcelona on a four-year contract. Manchester City is looking to replace him by pursuing Ayoub Bouaddi, Enzo Fernandez, Alex Scott, and Alexis McCallister. Negotiations with Bouaddi have started, and he has expressed willingness to join City.

Ahmad Ariaee-Nejad, the representative of Malayer, apologized for his offensive remarks about Mahsa Amini. He had previously described Mahsa Amini's death with the phrase "passed away." These remarks sparked widespread reactions.

Ahmad Alavi, an economist, spoke about the sale of Iran's oil to intermediaries and its impact on the country's economy. He said this indicates increased pressure from sanctions and difficulties in repatriating oil revenues. He also mentioned the rise in corruption and the transfer of financial resources abroad.

Doctors and teachers report issues with their salaries and bonuses. Flour shortages in bakeries have led to reduced bread quality. Some people face livelihood challenges due to unemployment and high inflation.

In recent days, Esteghlal and Persepolis clubs have mentioned Timsar Khosrowani and Ali Abdeh, the owners before the 1979 revolution, for the first time. The Islamic Republic had previously confiscated their properties and labeled them traitors. This topic was discussed in a conversation between Mazdak Mirzaei and Mohammad Taghavi on the Hat-trick program.

Esmaeil Baqaei stated that there is no 60-day deadline in the Islamabad agreement. He said the Islamic Republic does not make decisions based on ultimatums or deadlines, and the US violation of the agreement invalidated the 60-day period. Due to the extensive breach, no talks were initiated.
Yadollah Javani, the political deputy of the IRGC, stated that the Strait of Hormuz will open when the United States fulfills its commitments in the Islamabad agreement.

In Tehran, 165 hospitals require safety improvements due to safety issues. Forty hospitals have no safety certification, and several major hospitals like Sina and Imam Khomeini are in critical condition. The head of Tehran's City Council Safety Committee has warned about the dangers of this situation.

Amir Mohammad Karimi and Mahyar Eftekhari were expelled from the University of Tehran for burning the national flag during student protests. Their expulsion was confirmed by the disciplinary council of the Ministry of Science. This decision followed the university disciplinary committee's ruling.

Ismail Baghai, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, stated that until the status of the three missing army pilots is clarified, it means they have been captured. Iran's demand from Qatar to clarify the pilots' status is serious, and diplomatic efforts began from the first days of their disappearance. These pilots participated in a defensive operation against the origin of the US aggression.

Conflicts have occurred between Mohsen Khalili and Persepolis veterans. Veterans like Morteza Fonounizadeh reported the cessation of scouting salaries and their financial difficulties. These issues reflect the tough economic conditions faced by football veterans in Iran.

Masrour Barzani condemned the drone attacks by the Islamic Republic on his special office and the residence of the security chief as cowardly and unacceptable. He described these attacks as a direct threat to the security and stability of the Kurdistan Region. Barzani emphasized that these attacks will not prevent them from fulfilling their duties.

Gholamreza Nouri Ghezeljeh stated that Iran has not directly imported American-made goods but has purchased from international companies with American shareholders. Some of Iran's blocked funds in foreign banks can be used on the condition of buying food from these companies. He described this path as a way to use Iran's blocked resources.

A 13-year-old girl named Melika Hematzadeh died in Nikshahr hospital due to a scorpion sting and lack of medical facilities and medicine. The incident occurred in Desk village, Nikshahr county. The main cause of death was reported as shortage of medicine and medical facilities.

Two French diplomats were interrogated and beaten for five hours after a work meeting with two Iranian graphic designers. The Ministry of Intelligence described the meeting as a secret gathering and an example of infiltration. The two graphic designers present at the meeting remain in detention.

Today, Monday, 26 Mordad, employees of the South Pars Gas Complex held a protest gathering on platform 15. They demanded salary base adjustments and improvements in working conditions. The protest was held to address their demands.

Parisa Lashkari's daughter held her mother's birthday ceremony at her grave. Parisa Lashkari was killed during the protests on January 10, 2026, in Mamasani. These protests took place in Nurabad, Mamasani, Fars province.

A mother of a 15-year-old student said her daughter was expelled from the entrance exam for an art school due to not wearing the uniform. Despite wearing a headscarf, officials did not allow her to take the exam. The education authorities also responded to the mother's protest with insulting behavior.

A citizen of Gorgan reported that electricity is cut twice a day for two hours each time. Additionally, water is cut off from 6 PM to 6 AM for 12 hours. This issue was reported in a video to Iran International.

A resident of Bumehen reported daily two-hour power outages in the city. He attributed this situation to the rule of the Islamic Republic after fifty years. This report was sent to Iran International.

Mostafa Izadi, deputy commander of the IRGC, stated that there are no time or location restrictions in cyberspace and the world is thirsty for the teachings of the Islamic Revolution. He emphasized the need to organize efforts in this space to achieve victory. He also highlighted the importance of explaining the leadership characteristics of the Islamic Revolution in the soft war.

Workers and retirees complain about unpaid wages and arrears. Living costs have increased and rents have risen sharply. Issues such as power outages and removal of overtime pay have also affected working conditions.

Two Iranian attack drones targeted the offices of the Prime Minister and a senior security official of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq amid mediation efforts by the Kurdistan Region's president between Tehran and Washington. These attacks occurred during negotiations between the two sides. More details are provided in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

Khadijeh Mobaraki Dil, a teacher working in Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad province, was sentenced to mandatory retirement. This ruling was issued by the primary board for administrative violations of education staff in the province.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh stated that the conditions for the previous nuclear agreement no longer exist and distrust between Tehran and Washington has increased. He said the Islamic Republic cannot maintain the 'neither war nor negotiation' stance for long. If neither side retreats, the situation could move towards war.

Ali Tajernia, head of Esteghlal club, stated that this year's budget is lower in rial terms than last year. The expenses of the senior football team are also less than the reported figures. Additionally, Esteghlal's overall expenses are less than those of Persepolis.

A group of retired telecommunications workers held a protest in Sanandaj. The protest was due to unpaid claims, incomplete implementation of regulation 89/24, and poor supplementary insurance conditions. They demanded attention to these issues.

Ali Salehi, Tehran's prosecutor, stated that individuals who published a clip mocking the Arbaeen ceremony were immediately arrested. Additionally, dealing with offenses against public decency in some cafes and restaurants and stores selling inappropriate clothing is a priority for the judiciary.

The Tehran prosecutor announced intensified actions against cafes, restaurants, and stores accused of moral crimes or selling inappropriate clothing. Additionally, citizens' content on social media is continuously monitored by the Special Prosecutor's Office for Moral Security. This measure is seen as an expansion of surveillance over privacy and individual freedoms.

Danial Eiri, the 22-year-old defender from Nassaji, has joined Persepolis with a five-year contract. Persepolis paid 190 billion tomans for his transfer certificate. His contract will pay 77 billion tomans in the first year and about 700 billion tomans over five years.

Dozens of security forces of the Islamic Republic raided the village of Parchestan Gorooyi in Izeh county on Sunday night, August 16, and arrested three relatives of Kian Pirfalak's family. Jamshid Molaei was transferred to the hospital with a broken hand but was taken again to an unknown location. The families are unaware of the detainees' whereabouts and are deeply concerned about their health.

A woman and a man in Tehran were arrested for publishing a video described by the Tehran prosecutor as insulting to the Arbaeen ceremony. Their social media pages have also been blocked by judicial order.

The riverbed of Aligudarz in Lorestan province has been asphalted. The mayor of Aligudarz stated that this project was implemented to organize the riverbed, which had no permanent water for years. Part of the riverbed has been converted into a parking lot, weekly market, and urban space.

At least 19 people were killed in drone and missile attacks between Russia and Ukraine. A book market in Kyiv was destroyed, and a missile attack in Belgorod, Russia, resulted in at least six deaths. This information comes from Iran International's report.

The 60-day deadline of the Islamabad agreement for a comprehensive deal between Tehran and Washington ended on August 17 without official extension. Donald Trump told Fox News that the Islamic Republic should raise the white flag of surrender. More details are available in an interview with Maryam Rahmati.

The gas connection of the Amjadieh sports complex has been cut off due to a debt of over 2 billion tomans to the gas department. The Wrestling Federation has also faced a power cut at the Azadi sports complex due to a 22 billion toman debt. The Amjadieh sports complex is a subsidiary of the Sports Facilities Development and Maintenance Company.
Younes Azadbar, a resident of Rasht, was released on Monday, August 26, after posting bail of 1.5 billion tomans. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

In 2004, a 16-year-old girl named Atefeh Sahaaleh was publicly executed for extramarital sex. She was arrested based on local testimony and her grandfather's complaint. Before the execution, she had received over 300 lashes.

Nirvana Torbati Nejad, a detained citizen, was released today, Monday, 26 Mordad, on bail from Amirabad Prison in Gorgan. Her release was carried out with the attorney Ramazan Haji Mashhadi and by posting bail to the investigative branch of the General and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office in Gorgan. This news was reported by HRANA news agency.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf described the agreement between Iran and the US as a document of pride and victory in diplomacy. He emphasized that the US and Israel failed to achieve their goals in the recent war and that Iran emerged victorious. Ghalibaf added that the Iranian nation bravely stood firm in this war.

Sixty experts, business activists, and parliament members attribute the price increases in Iran's economy to the removal of preferential currency for essential goods imports. Arash Azarmi calls the disputes a distraction and points to the political governance of the Islamic Republic as the root of the crisis. Heavy inflation has increased household costs and worsened the livelihood crisis.

A senior Iranian official told Reuters that if diplomacy fails, all Iranian institutions are ready to escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and the region. Tehran has set a deadline of several weeks for the full implementation of the agreement by the US. The official added that Tehran will not wait indefinitely to continue the naval blockade against the US.

On the eve of the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Zhina Amini's death, insulting remarks by a member of parliament about her have sparked widespread reactions on social media and from Mahsa's family. The Amini family has defended her name and status. This report was published by Adaleh Borang from Iran International.

Melika Hematzadeh, a 13-year-old girl from Nikshahr, died after a scorpion sting and lack of medical facilities in the hospital. Her family had to transfer her by private car due to the absence of an ambulance and medical equipment. Hospitals also lacked the necessary blood platelets, and timely treatment was not provided.

Manouchehr Motaki spoke in a meeting about the possibility of a ground war with the US, saying American soldiers' bodies would not be returned to their families. He added that capturing a US base in Iraq, Kuwait, or Bahrain could determine the outcome of the war. These statements were made in an official session.

A state TV presenter responded to criticism about airstrikes on southern Iran by saying, "Southern Iran is sacrificed for southern Lebanon." This statement sparked strong reactions on social media. The state news agency released a longer video of her remarks.

Ali Khazarian stated that the resistance front is stronger today than ever, and Hezbollah's operations against Israel have increased. He emphasized the need to compensate for the weakening of the resistance in the Syrian front. He also said the resistance movement is in its strongest period and should focus on advancement.

Iran International has called on its audience to write about the impact of the December protests on their lives. Responses indicate that these protests have changed many citizens' perceptions of the future. More details are provided in an interview with Farnoush Faraji.

Jared Kushner held a meeting with Benjamin Netanyahu and Isaac Herzog regarding the Gaza plan. Kushner, in a meeting lasting over four hours, urged Netanyahu to advance the Gaza ceasefire plan supported by Donald Trump and not to obstruct it.

Donald Trump stated that the US has direct communication channels with Iran's Revolutionary Guard officials. He also said Iran must surrender and that the US naval blockade is increasing economic pressure. The Revolutionary Guard spokesperson denied this claim and called it a delusion.

Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei announced that in his new term as head, some judicial officials will be changed or relocated. The goal is to increase dynamism and improve service delivery to the people. He emphasized that these changes should not be interpreted otherwise.

Ali Al-Zaidi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, held a meeting with the country's oil ministry officials to discuss ways to counter the effects of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the reduction of oil exports. He called for accelerating the reconstruction and development of oil pipelines. Cooperation with international companies for marketing and selling Iraqi oil was also emphasized.

A man in Qaemshahr killed his wife and young daughter. The suspect confessed to the murders after being arrested. The Qaemshahr prosecutor said the man tried to stage the scene to make the deaths appear as gas leakage.

The Israeli Prime Minister's office announced that Benjamin Netanyahu and the peace delegation agreed to form two working groups regarding Gaza. The first group will focus on disarmament and demilitarization of Gaza and must be completed before reconstruction begins. The second group will address health issues and clean water supply in Gaza.

A secret contact between the US government and the commander of the IRGC has been confirmed. Trump has asked Tehran to surrender at the end of the 60-day deadline for an agreement. The Israeli website Ynet also reported on the IRGC's dominance over the Islamic Republic.

The Minister of Roads stated that about 100 aircraft were damaged in the war, with 8 completely destroyed. Additionally, around 140 private non-military vessels were also damaged. These vessels include local cargo and passenger transport boats used by coastal residents.

The Israeli Prime Minister told Jared Kushner that Israel will not withdraw its forces from Gaza or allow reconstruction until Hamas is fully disarmed. An American general will oversee the disarmament process of Hamas. Hamas demands an end to Israeli attacks and troop withdrawal before disarming.

The documentary drama "Court of History" examines Iran after the Islamic Republic and how to deal with its crimes. The film will be broadcast on Thursday, August 20 at 8:00 PM Tehran time on Iran International. A repeat will air on Friday, August 21 at 11:00 AM.

The Uzbekistan national football team will play against Iran on September 24, 1405 (Persian calendar) in Tashkent. They will then face Argentina in China on September 30 and play against South Korea on October 6. This will be the eighth match between Iran and Uzbekistan during Ghalenoei's era.

The US Department of Defense announced it has ordered 30 US academic institutions to immediately and comprehensively review their academic, financial, and research collaborations with foreign entities of concern to Washington. The stated goal is to prevent unauthorized technology transfer, intellectual property theft, and foreign exploitation of research funded by American taxpayers. The institutions must report their findings and actions by 9 Shahrivar to maintain eligibility for future federal research funding.

The Islamic Consultative Assembly is reviewing a plan called the "Countering Infiltration Plan" that could restrict and securitize communication with foreign media, universities, and institutions. This plan may place Iranian citizens' connections with the world under the supervision of the Ministry of Intelligence. Concerns have been raised about the impact of this plan on the future of Iran's young generation.

Mehdi Ahmadi, the host of the program 'Azad,' has been summoned to the prosecutor's office on charges of spreading falsehoods. He was released on bail according to judicial orders. The 'Azad' media outlet is banned from publishing interviews until further notice.
The spokesperson of the political and press courts jury announced that the manager of the news site Serat News was found guilty by the press court.

Khatoun Bam football team lost 3-0 to CSKA Dushanbe in their first match of the AFC Women's Champions League qualifiers. The goals were scored by Sara Didar and Maryam Dini. Khatoun Bam topped the group with this victory and will play against Al-Nassr Saudi Arabia on Thursday.

Tom Barrack, the US Ambassador to Turkey, strongly condemned the attack on Masrour Barzani, Prime Minister of the Kurdistan Region, and his office in Erbil, calling it a direct threat to regional stability. He wrote on X that aggression against trusted Kurdish allies is unacceptable and Washington will not tolerate such actions. Barrack also expressed full US support for Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's leadership in restoring full national sovereignty.
At 19:30 on Monday, 26 Mordad, a fire broke out in shops around Golestan Municipality Square. Images of the incident have been received. No further details have been announced.

Jared Kushner, Tony Blair, and Nikolay Mladenov met with Benjamin Netanyahu as part of efforts to advance the peace process in Gaza. This meeting took place after their meeting with Hamas representatives. The report was provided by Babak Es-haqi from Iran International.

Pierre Poilievre, leader of Canada's Conservative Party, called for the immediate expulsion of agents affiliated with the IRGC from Canada. He also announced coordination for a meeting with Prince Reza Pahlavi. These statements were made at a meeting with Iranians in Vancouver.

Three prisoners sentenced to death in Varamin, Saravan, and Bardasir were spared execution following the consent of the victims' families. This news was reported by Harana News Agency. More details are provided in the continuation of the report.

Behnam Taleblu stated that the 60-day agreement between the Islamic Republic and the US over the Strait of Hormuz lasted only two to three weeks. He considered the diplomatic deadlock predictable. There is a possibility of a military reaction from the Islamic Republic in the coming weeks.

The 25-year prison sentence of Omid Bayat Sarmadi was overturned by the Supreme Court. His case has been referred to a peer branch for re-examination. He was previously sentenced to 25 years in prison by the Tehran Revolutionary Court.

The Islamabad agreement period has ended, and there are few signs of its renewal. One reason is the secret plan of the Islamic Republic to expand the war. This issue was reported by the Wall Street Journal.

The first deputy of Pezeshkian announced that the government, in coordination with security institutions, has set a fourth gasoline price. Mohammad Reza Aref said this plan was supposed to be tested in Kerman province. The 87,000 toman price implemented in Kerman differs from the approved rate.

Ali Al-Zaidi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, announced the formation of a committee to investigate the attack on Masrour Barzani's office. The Kurdistan Region condemned the attack as inconsistent with good neighborliness and criticized the Islamic Republic's behavior. The Kurdistan Region emphasized that this conflict is not part of regional conflicts.

The nonprofit organization FracSquare has requested FIFA's governance committee to declare Gianni Infantino ineligible for re-election as FIFA president. The organization accused Infantino of repeated violations of FIFA's duties and called for an investigation into the awarding of the FIFA Peace Prize to Donald Trump. Infantino's presidency has faced controversies and scandals following these allegations.

About 280 workers at the Siaadan Abhar steel factory have not received one month of wages and several months of insurance payments. Workers at the Iran Shahr steam power plant have also reported wage arrears. Pars Khodro retirees have been waiting for six months for part of their severance pay.

CENTCOM announced that the USS Mason destroyer is enforcing the US Iron Wall blockade against Iran. By August 17, US forces have altered the routes of 64 commercial ships, disabled three ships, and boarded two ships.

The cost of the livelihood basket for an average working-class family has reached 90 million tomans per month. This amount has more than doubled compared to last March when it was 43 million tomans. The income of the majority of the working class is less than half of this amount.
A man in Tehran committed acid attacks on two of his wife's colleagues due to suspicion. He was tried by the Tehran criminal court. This incident took place in Tehran.
Trump confirmed having a direct channel with the IRGC. He threatened Tehran with surrender and bombing Oman. This was mentioned in the audio version of Titraval with Niusha Saremi.

The nonprofit organization Foursquare has requested FIFA to declare Gianni Infantino ineligible for re-election as FIFA president. The group accuses Infantino of repeatedly violating political neutrality and causing multiple controversies. Foursquare also called for an investigation into the awarding of the FIFA Peace Prize to Donald Trump.

Donald Trump said he asked South Korea to help the US regarding Iran, but they refused. He emphasized that the US has 39,000 troops in South Korea protecting them against North Korea. Trump also stated that Iran will not accept the agreement that the US deems necessary.

Donald Trump stated that the United States is not seeking to extend the agreement with the Islamic Republic. He also said that the Islamic Republic will not make the agreement that the US requires. These remarks were made at the White House.

The leader of Canada's Conservative Party criticized the federal government and called for the immediate dismissal of those voluntarily cooperating with the IRGC. He emphasized that conscripts should not be targeted as they are victims of this terrorist organization. He also announced coordination for a meeting with Prince Reza Pahlavi and an official invitation for him to visit Canada.

A senior Iranian official stated that Tehran has given the US only a few weeks to fulfill its commitments under the agreement. After this period, precise and timely military actions will be taken. The political deputy of the IRGC also conditioned the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz on the US fulfilling its commitments.

Kevin Lamour, FIFA's Chief Operating Officer, left the organization less than three weeks after strongly criticizing the canceled plan to sell FIFA competition shares. FIFA confirmed the end of cooperation with Lamour on August 17, 2026, and thanked him. FIFA has not commented on reports of his dismissal.
Donald Trump, responding to a question about Oman and the Strait of Hormuz, said he does not think Oman has behaved very well, but the United States will deal with them very easily.

The film "Bidad" directed by Sohail Beiraghi was released on YouTube without official permission. The film focuses on the ban on women's singing in Iran. The judiciary had previously issued rulings against the filmmakers.

The Appeals Court of Fars Province confirmed the 15-month prison sentence and additional penalties for Mehdi Fathi. He was also sentenced to travel ban, passport cancellation, and two years of prohibition from online activities. This sentence was previously issued by the Revolutionary Court of Shiraz.

Jared Kushner, the US president's special envoy, said Hamas leaders at the rare Cairo meeting expressed positive positions but trust in the group remains difficult and its adherence to commitments must be tested in practice. He added that the process of disarmament and demilitarization of Gaza could begin within 30 days, and reconstruction will not start before that. Kushner also said that if Hamas does not hand over its weapons and tunnels within the next 60 to 90 days, US support for the continuation of Israeli operations will increase.

Many people faced system disruptions and long queues when trying to verify residency and receive ration cards. The Ministry of Cooperatives has requested residency verification by the end of September, otherwise ration card payments will be stopped. The deputy of cooperation in Sistan and Baluchestan advised completing the process online.

Morad Vaisi stated that the Islamic Republic has entered a turbulent 80-day period. This period has started now and will continue until the US elections. He mentioned severe economic pressures, a high possibility of broader conflict with the US, and a renewed uprising by the people.

Morad Veisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, criticized the Islamic Republic's strategy against the US and Israel as fundamentally flawed. He stated that the Islamic Republic assumes the US and Israel are unaware of its plans, which is not true. He also pointed out the mistake of hoping for no attack until the US elections.

Kataib Hezbollah Iraq called Mohammed Shia al-Sudani reckless for pressuring militias and threatened retaliatory action. The group set conditions for disarmament talks. The conditions include the withdrawal of American and Turkish forces and the dissolution of the Peshmerga.

Donald Trump welcomed the idea of declaring the Strait of Hormuz as US territory and said Washington controls the waterway through a naval blockade. He warned that the Islamic Republic is in a difficult economic and military situation. Trump added that Iran still has the ability to cause disruptions, including mining ships' paths.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, identified internal crises and a daily shortage of 15 to 20 million liters of gasoline as major challenges for the Islamic Republic until the US elections. He warned that these crises could lead to social unrest and threaten the regime's survival. He also mentioned the US blockade preventing gasoline imports.

The Asian Football Confederation announced that the deadline for Esteghlal club to introduce a hosting stadium in the Elite League of Asia has ended. The football federations of Iraq and Uzbekistan did not give final approval for Esteghlal's hosting. AFC will make the final decision regarding Esteghlal's hosting stadium.

The Coalition of Iranian Kurdish Political Forces condemned the drone attacks by the Islamic Republic on the office of the Prime Minister of Iraqi Kurdistan and the security organization headquarters. The coalition described these attacks as a violation of Iraq's sovereignty and a threat to the security of the Kurdistan Region. They called for an immediate halt to the attacks and serious action from the Iraqi government and diplomatic countries.

FIFA released images of the 2026 World Cup final between Spain and Argentina from the perspective of the referee, Slavko Vinčić. These images include moments from the match and the referee's interactions with players. More details of these scenes can be found on FIFA's website.

Donald Trump said the Islamic Republic must give up acquiring nuclear weapons and until then, the US will continue economic blockade and control of the Strait of Hormuz to pressure Tehran. He emphasized that despite the Strait of Hormuz being open, the US naval blockade has been effective and prevented the Islamic Republic from using this waterway. Trump added that Washington is ready to intensify its actions if necessary and described the Islamic Republic's economic situation and military capability as very weak.

Donald Trump stated that South Korea rejected the US request to participate in military operations against the Islamic Republic. He criticized this decision and questioned why the US should spend billions defending South Korea while Seoul refuses to support militarily. Trump also said some other US allies, including NATO members, do not participate in protecting the Strait of Hormuz.
